page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with an italic scripture quotation at the top. No margin notes. Running head at the top right, page number at the top left. Catchword at the lower right.

p.i: pse dominabitur tui. Ada vero dixit, Quia audisti vocem vxoris tuæ, & comedi disti de ligno, ex quo præceperam tibi ne comederes, maledicta terra propter te, in laboribus comedes ex ea cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ: spinas & tribulos germinabit tibi, & comedes herbas terræ. In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane, donec reuertaris in terram, de qua sumptus es: quia puluis es, & in pulverem reuerteris.

main_text.p: 1 Est hoc in more positum institutoque maiorum, vt testari volentibus coram eccle-sia Christiana, se coniuges esse, præleguntur quædam capita ex verbo Dei, ne videlicet illud vitæ genus honestum & laudabile ingrediantur absque scientia & intellectu Dei & verbi eius, quemadmodum infideles face-re solent: de quibus Raphael angelus Tob. 6. Hi namque qui coniugium (inquit) ita fuscipiunt, vt Deum à se & à sua mente exclu-dant, & suæ libidini ita vacent, ficut equus & mulus, quibus non est intellectus, habet potestatem dæmonium super eos.

2 Sunt autem sex capita, quæ illis potissimum proponuntur: idque à ministris Ecclesiæ: quos ante 1000. [?] annos publico ritu nouos coniuges coniunxisse, ex Nicephoro lib.14.cap.55 apparet. vbi Synefius dicit, Deum & leges, & sacram Theophili manum, v

page.notes: The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The italic passage is Genesis 3:16–19 as printed; the printed word "Ada" is read as shown, and the swash initials of "Ada" and "Quia" are read as plain letters. "1000" is printed in old-style figures that look like "1ooo"; read as 1000 with [?]. The last line ends at "manum, v" and the rest of the word, "xorem", stands as catchword at the foot. "fuscipiunt" and "face-re" carry the printed line-end breaks; the break in "fuscipiunt" has no visible hyphen, so it is written whole. Page number and running head are printed at the top: "16" left, "CONCIONES" right.
